actions: depresses and stabilizes the clavicle at the sternoclavicular joint

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Small, deeply-placed muscle beneath the clavicle; cushions the subclavian vessels immediately below it from the bone during clavicle fracture, a clinically relevant protective relationship.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Linear probe placed longitudinally along the inferior surface of the clavicle, in the infraclavicular fossa, to bring this muscle's short belly into view running from the clavicle's undersurface toward the first rib/costal cartilage.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Immediately deep to the clavicle and the clavipectoral fascia, superficial to the subclavian vessels and brachial plexus (which lie deep and slightly caudal/medial to it) -- real-time ultrasound guidance is used specifically to keep the needle out of that neurovascular plane.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Small, short, band-like muscle directly under the clavicle's acoustic shadow; contracts (visible on dynamic scanning) with shoulder depression/retraction.
structures_at_risk: subclavian artery and vein, deep and slightly caudal to the muscle

brachial plexus, deep and lateral to the muscle -- the reason this and the other injections in the same series (anterior scalene, pectoralis minor) were done under real-time ultrasound rather than landmark technique
pleura/apex of lung, deep to the neurovascular bundle
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Genuine clinical finding: ultrasound-guided botulinum toxin injection of subclavius (along with anterior scalene and pectoralis minor) is a real, described technique for neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome (NTOS), where an overactive/hypertrophied subclavius is one of several muscles thought to compress the brachial plexus. In this retrospective series of 41 subjects, only 1 of 92 total injections targeted subclavius specifically (58 anterior scalene, 33 pectoralis minor, 1 subclavius) -- so while the technique and rationale are real and specific to this muscle, the direct clinical experience with it is limited to a single reported case within that series. No dedicated motor-point/neural-arborization mapping study for this muscle was found.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Torriani M, Gupta R, Donahue DM (2010) 'Botulinum toxin injection in neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome: results and experience using a ultrasound-guided approach', Skeletal Radiol 39(10):973-980, doi:10.1007/s00256-010-0897-1
